explanation: The standard free energy change is tied directly to the equilibrium constant by dG° = -R*T*ln(K), where R = 8.314 J/(mol K) and T is in kelvin. A negative dG° forces ln K positive, so K > 1 and products are favored; a positive dG° gives K < 1 (reactants favored); and dG° = 0 means K = 1 at equilibrium. Because the relationship is logarithmic, even modest changes in dG° swing K by orders of magnitude. On the AP exam you rearrange to K = exp(-dG°/RT), keeping dG° in J (not kJ) to match R; the graph plots ln K versus dG° as a straight line through the origin.
bullets: dG° = 0 → K = 1, the reaction sits at equilibrium.
Unit match: dG° in J/mol with R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
Logarithmic link: small dG° shifts move K by powers of 10.
